summary: PPPMKokkos shadows PPPM::gc and never overrides PPPM::reset_grid(), so a load-balance rebalance runs the CPU reset_grid on the KOKKOS style: it calls the non-virtual PPPM::compute_rho_coeff(), which writes the base rho_coeff array that a KOKKOS run never allocates (nullptr), and dereferences the base gc, which is also nullptr.
evidence:
src/KOKKOS/pppm_kokkos.cpp:103-108:
  // same name but different than base class
  gc = nullptr; fft1 = nullptr; fft2 = nullptr; remap = nullptr;
(these assign the PPPMKokkos members declared in src/KOKKOS/pppm_kokkos.h:449, which shadow PPPM::gc etc.; PPPM's own gc is set to nullptr at src/KSPACE/pppm.cpp:80 and never re-assigned in a KOKKOS run).  'grep -rn reset_grid src/KOKKOS' finds nothing, so PPPM::reset_grid (src/KSPACE/pppm.cpp:637-668) is inherited unchanged; it runs
  allocate();                                   // virtual -> PPPMKokkos::allocate, which creates only k_rho_coeff (pppm_kokkos.cpp:865) and never memory->create2d_offset(rho_coeff,...) as PPPM::allocate does at pppm.cpp:913
  if (!overlap_allowed && !gc->ghost_adjacent()) // base gc == nullptr
  compute_rho_coeff();                          // NOT virtual (src/KSPACE/pppm.h:142) -> PPPM::compute_rho_coeff writes 'rho_coeff[l][m] = a[l][k];' (pppm.cpp:2930) with rho_coeff == nullptr
reset_grid() is called on every rebalance: src/fix_balance.cpp:341 'if (force->kspace) force->kspace->reset_grid();'.
failure_scenario: 'fix balance ... rcb' (or shift) in a run with kspace_style pppm/kk: the rebalance calls kspace->reset_grid(), which segfaults in PPPM::compute_rho_coeff (null rho_coeff); with 'kspace_modify overlap no' it segfaults one line earlier on the null base gc.  Even if the pointers were valid, the KOKKOS device copies (k_rho_coeff / d_rho_coeff, re-created uninitialized by PPPMKokkos::allocate) would never be filled or synced, since PPPMKokkos::init() is the only place that does compute_rho_coeff() + k_rho_coeff.modify_host()/sync (pppm_kokkos.cpp:277-281).
suggested_fix: Give PPPMKokkos an override of reset_grid() that mirrors PPPM::reset_grid but uses the KOKKOS gc and calls PPPMKokkos::compute_rho_coeff() followed by k_rho_coeff.modify_host()/sync<DeviceType>(); alternatively make PPPM::compute_rho_coeff virtual and stop shadowing gc.  NOTE: pppm_kokkos.cpp is outside this reviewer's assigned file list (found while tracing Grid3dKokkos callers).

summary: unpack_forward_grid_kokkos's per-atom branch reads the u_brick (per-atom energy) value from d_buf[7*i] without adding unpack_offset, unlike the six virial reads right below it, so the tiled grid comm unpacks the wrong buffer stretch.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/pppm_kokkos.cpp:2418 'if (eflag_atom) d_u_brick(iz,iy,ix) = d_buf[7*i];' versus :2420-2425 'd_v0_brick(iz,iy,ix) = d_buf[7*i+1 + unpack_offset]; ... d_v5_brick(iz,iy,ix) = d_buf[7*i+6 + unpack_offset];' and the sibling kernel :2404-2406 'd_vdx_brick(iz,iy,ix) = d_buf[3*i   + unpack_offset];'.  unpack_offset is set from the caller at :2379 and the tiled path passes a non-zero value: src/KOKKOS/grid3d_kokkos.cpp:771-773 'offset = nper * recv[m].offset; kspaceKKBase->unpack_forward_grid_kokkos(which,k_buf2,offset,recv[m].nunpack,k_recv_unpacklist,m);'.  The CPU base advances one running index for every field (src/KSPACE/pppm.cpp, PPPM::unpack_forward_grid, FORWARD_IK_PERATOM branch: 'if (eflag_atom) esrc[list[i]] = buf[n++];').
failure_scenario: comm_style tiled (Comm::LAYOUT_TILED) with 'kspace_style pppm/kk' and any per-atom energy request (compute pe/atom, dump custom c_pe), on a run with more than one received message: every receive after the first fills its ghost u_brick cells from the beginning of the shared receive buffer instead of its own stretch -> wrong per-atom Coulomb energies (and reads past the end of the buffer for the last receive is avoided only by luck).
suggested_fix: Change the line to 'if (eflag_atom) d_u_brick(iz,iy,ix) = d_buf[7*i + unpack_offset];'.

summary: PPPMKokkos::init() never implements the 'kspace_modify slab auto' iteration, so slab_volfactor stays at its 1.0 initial value and the EW3DC slab correction is applied to a box with no inserted vacuum.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/pppm_kokkos.cpp:221-252 runs only the plain 'while (order >= minorder)' loop with no reference to slab_auto, while the CPU base wraps it in the auto-volfactor loop: src/KSPACE/pppm.cpp:295-298 'const bool slab_auto_enabled = (slabflag == 1 && slab_auto); if (slab_auto_enabled) slab_volfactor = auto_slab_volfactor(accuracy, two_charge_force, g_ewald, xprd, yprd, zprd, error);' and :354-360 which re-derives it after adjust_gewald() until converged.  'kspace_modify slab auto' is accepted for any pppmflag style and sets 'slabflag = 1; slab_auto = 1; slab_volfactor = 1.0;' (src/kspace.cpp:527-530); nothing in PPPMKokkos rejects it.
failure_scenario: 'kspace_style pppm/kk' plus 'kspace_modify slab auto': slab_volfactor remains 1.0, so zprd_slab == zprd, Grid3d::set_zfactor(1.0) inserts no vacuum, and slabcorr() adds the EW3DC dipole correction for a slab geometry that was never extended -> silently wrong energies and z forces (the identical CPU input picks a volfactor of typically 3).
suggested_fix: Either port the slab_auto convergence loop from PPPM::init() into PPPMKokkos::init(), or explicitly error out in PPPMKokkos::init() when (slabflag == 1 && slab_auto).

summary: deallocate() nulls fft1 twice and never nulls fft2, leaving fft2 a dangling pointer after the FFT3dKokkos object is deleted.
failure_scenario: Any path that calls deallocate() twice without an intervening allocate() double-frees fft2: e.g. PPPMKokkos::init() calls deallocate() at :212 and error->all()s at :254/:256 before reaching allocate() at :272, after which the destructor (:127) calls deallocate() again -> delete of an already freed FFT3dKokkos.
suggested_fix: Replace the second 'fft1 = nullptr;' with 'fft2 = nullptr;'.

summary: For triclinic boxes compute() converts x to lamda coordinates through DomainKokkos, which always runs on the device and marks X_MASK modified on Device, so the pppm/kk/host instantiation keeps reading the un-converted host coordinates.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/pppm_kokkos.cpp:590 'x = atomKK->k_x.view<DeviceType>();' and :620 'domain->x2lamda(atomKK->nlocal);' with no atomKK->sync afterwards.  DomainKokkos::x2lamda(int n) (src/KOKKOS/domain_kokkos.cpp:672-685) does 'atomKK->sync(Device,X_MASK); x = atomKK->k_x.view_device(); ... Kokkos::parallel_for(Kokkos::RangePolicy<LMPDeviceType, TagDomain_x2lamda>(0,n),*this); ... atomKK->modified(Device,X_MASK);' - always LMPDeviceType.  src/KOKKOS/pppm_kokkos.h:18 registers 'KSpaceStyle(pppm/kk/host,PPPMKokkos<LMPHostType>);', whose kernels then read the host mirror.
failure_scenario: GPU build, triclinic box, 'kspace_style pppm/kk/host': particle_map()/make_rho()/fieldforce_ik() index the grid with Cartesian coordinates while boxlo has been set to domain->boxlo_lamda (:616-618), so every atom maps to a nonsense grid point -> 'Out of range atoms - cannot compute PPPM' or badly wrong long-range forces.
suggested_fix: Call 'atomKK->sync(execution_space,X_MASK);' after domain->x2lamda() (and again after domain->lamda2x()), or refuse triclinic for the host instantiation.

summary: deallocate() passes the plain device Views to memoryKK->destroy_kokkos() instead of the DualViews the buffers were created from, so k_density_fft/k_work1/k_work2 keep holding their allocations.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/pppm_kokkos.cpp:906-908 'memoryKK->destroy_kokkos(d_density_fft,density_fft); memoryKK->destroy_kokkos(d_work1,work1); memoryKK->destroy_kokkos(d_work2,work2);' whereas allocate() created them through the DualViews: :835-842 'memoryKK->create_kokkos(k_density_fft,density_fft,nfft_both,...); d_density_fft = k_density_fft.view<DeviceType>(); ... memoryKK->create_kokkos(k_work1,work1,2*nfft_both,...);'.  destroy_kokkos only does 'data = TYPE(); array = nullptr;' (src/KOKKOS/memory_kokkos.h:83-88), so the DualView reference keeps the memory alive until the next create_kokkos overwrites it.
failure_scenario: On PPPMKokkos::init() (which calls deallocate() at :212 and allocate() at :272) the old grid-sized FFT work arrays are still referenced by k_work1/k_work2/k_density_fft while the new ones are allocated -> transient doubling of the FFT buffer footprint; on a memory-tight GPU this is an out-of-memory abort where the CPU build succeeds.
suggested_fix: Pass the DualViews: 'memoryKK->destroy_kokkos(k_density_fft,density_fft);' etc., and reset the derived device views to empty.

summary: k_eatom/k_vatom are destroyed and re-created on every compute() call whenever per-atom energy/virial is requested, instead of only when the existing view is too small.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/pppm_kokkos.cpp:576-585 'if (eflag_atom) { memoryKK->destroy_kokkos(k_eatom,eatom); memoryKK->create_kokkos(k_eatom,eatom,maxeatom,"pair:eatom"); d_eatom = k_eatom.view<DeviceType>(); }' with no size test.  Every other KOKKOS style guards it, e.g. src/KOKKOS/pair_lj_cut_kokkos.cpp 'if (k_eatom.extent(0) < maxeatom) { destroy; create; ... } else Kokkos::deep_copy(d_eatom,0.0);', and the CPU base only reallocates when 'atom->nmax > maxeatom' (src/kspace.cpp, KSpace::ev_setup).
failure_scenario: A run with 'compute pe/atom' or 'compute stress/atom' and 'kspace_style pppm/kk' performs two device allocations plus two frees (each an implicit fence) per timestep, which on a GPU costs far more than the kernels themselves.
suggested_fix: Reallocate only when 'k_eatom.extent(0) < maxeatom' and otherwise Kokkos::deep_copy the view to zero.

verified_by: orchestrator (read code directly) (partial: no reset_grid override and non-virtual compute_rho_coeff confirmed; allocate/gc details from group 06)
summary: PPPMKokkos does not override reset_grid(), so a load-balance rebalance runs PPPM::reset_grid, which calls the non-virtual PPPM::compute_rho_coeff() (writing the base rho_coeff array a KOKKOS run never allocates) and uses the base-class gc pointer that PPPMKokkos shadows and leaves null.
evidence: grep reset_grid pppm_kokkos.cpp: none; src/KSPACE/pppm.h:35 'void reset_grid() override;', :142 'void compute_rho_coeff();' (non-virtual); pppm_kokkos.cpp:2512 defines its own compute_rho_coeff. src/fix_balance.cpp calls kspace->reset_grid().
failure_scenario: fix balance with kspace_style pppm/kk -> segfault in PPPM::compute_rho_coeff (null rho_coeff) or on the null gc.
suggested_fix: Add a PPPMKokkos::reset_grid() override mirroring PPPM::reset_grid with the KOKKOS gc and compute_rho_coeff + k_rho_coeff sync, or make compute_rho_coeff virtual and stop shadowing gc.

summary: In the per-atom forward-unpack kernel the u_brick read omits unpack_offset ('d_buf[7*i]') while all six virial reads on the next lines include it, so with comm_style tiled every receive after the first fills its ghost per-atom energy cells from the wrong stretch of the shared buffer.
verified_by: orchestrator (src/KOKKOS/pppm_kokkos.cpp:2418 vs :2420-2425, and the sibling kernel at :2404-2406 which does include the offset).

summary: deallocate() sets fft1 = nullptr twice and never nulls fft2, so fft2 stays dangling after deletion and a second deallocate() without an intervening allocate() double-frees it (reachable through the error paths in init()).
verified_by: orchestrator (src/KOKKOS/pppm_kokkos.cpp:910-915: 'delete fft1; fft1 = nullptr; delete fft2; fft1 = nullptr;').

summary: grow_arrays() unconditionally refills the host mirrors of the tied per-atom DualViews from the device copies during a run, which silently discards the base class' host-side bookkeeping whenever the arrays grow on the HOST exchange/borders path of a GPU build.
failure_scenario: GPU build, `fix rigid/small/kk` on the host exchange path -- which init() selects automatically for ellipsoid/line/tri/body atom styles or whenever another per-atom fix (e.g. fix property/atom) lacks device exchange (fix_rigid_small_kokkos.cpp:170-181).  A reneighbor in which comm->exchange() or comm->borders() grows atom->nmax resets bodytag/bodyown/xcmimage/displace to their values from before the migration; pre_neighbor() then pushes that corrupted host state to the device, so migrated atoms keep the body IDs of the atoms that used to occupy their slots.  Result is either the hard error "Rigid body atoms ... missing on proc" from reset_atom2body(), or silently wrong body membership and wrong trajectories.
suggested_fix: Before the grow_kokkos() calls, push the host side to the device (modify_host() + sync<DeviceType>()) whenever the fix is running on the host exchange path -- or, more simply, extend host_holds_bookkeeping to also cover `!(exchange_comm_device && !commKK->exchange_comm_legacy)` so the existing save/restore of the host contents covers a grow during a host exchange too.

summary: On the first run, sort_kokkos() and setup_pre_neighbor() clear the DualView sync state and re-declare the (pre-exchange) host arrays authoritative, discarding the per-atom body bookkeeping that the setup-time DEVICE exchange legitimately moved; the justifying comment ("nothing had pushed the host arrays create_bodies() wrote to the device") is contradicted by pack_exchange_kokkos.
failure_scenario: Two or more MPI ranks, GPU build with the device exchange active, and at least one atom migrating during the setup-time comm->exchange() of the first run (e.g. a data file whose atoms lie outside the box, so domain->pbc() moves them across a proc boundary).  The per-atom bodytag the exchange moved on the device is thrown away and the pre-exchange host array -- indexed by the pre-exchange local atom ordering -- is used instead, so setup_bodies_static() builds the bodies from bodytags belonging to the wrong atoms: either the hard error "Rigid body atoms ... missing on proc" from reset_atom2body(), or silently wrong bodies and inertia tensors.
suggested_fix: On the first run, retire the device claim with sync_host() (which brings the exchange result down to the host) instead of clear_sync_state(), or only clear when the setup-time exchange actually packed nothing.

summary: The Langevin device kernel calls the unqualified C library sqrt() instead of Kokkos::sqrt(), which the KOKKOS package rules require for device kernels.
evidence:
src/KOKKOS/fix_rigid_small_kokkos.cpp:896-925, inside `Kokkos::parallel_for("fix rigid/small langevin", Range1D(0, nlocal_body), KOKKOS_LAMBDA(const int ibody) {`:
      double gamma2 = sqrt(b.mass) * tsqrt * sqrt(24.0*boltz/tp/dt/mvv2e) / ftm2v;   (:903)
      gamma2 = tsqrt * sqrt(24.0*boltz/tp/dt/mvv2e) / ftm2v;                          (:909)
      tbody[0] = static_cast<KK_FLOAT>(b.inertia[0]*gamma1*... + sqrt(b.inertia[0])*gamma2*(rand_gen.drand()-0.5));  (:921, :923, :925)
.github/instructions/kokkos.instructions.md requires Kokkos:: math inside device kernels; the rest of this file correctly routes its math through MathExtraKokkos::.
failure_scenario: Compiles on CUDA/HIP today because ::sqrt is provided as a device function, but is not portable to backends/toolchains where only the Kokkos:: wrappers are guaranteed, and blocks a future switch of these accumulators to KK_FLOAT.
suggested_fix: Replace the five in-kernel sqrt() calls with Kokkos::sqrt().

summary: The destructor frees the extended per-atom arrays only when extended/orientflag/dorientflag are still set; because setup_bodies_static() recomputes those flags on every reinit run, a flag that has flipped back to 0 leaves a Kokkos-owned pointer in the base class, which FixRigidSmall::~FixRigidSmall() then passes to memory->destroy().
failure_scenario: A `fix rigid/small/kk` with reinit yes whose bodies contain finite-size particles in run 1 but only point particles in a later run (the finite-size particles were deleted, or their radius set to 0): extended goes 1 -> 0, the destructor skips destroy_kokkos, and FixRigidSmall::~FixRigidSmall() calls memory->destroy() (sfree) on the host mirror of a Kokkos DualView -> heap corruption / crash at the end of the run.
suggested_fix: Guard on the pointers rather than the flags: `if (eflags) memoryKK->destroy_kokkos(k_eflags, eflags);` and likewise for orient/dorient.

summary: Five non-ASCII characters (RIGHTWARDS ARROW U+2192, EM DASH U+2014, RIGHT SINGLE QUOTATION MARK U+2019) appear in source comments in three KOKKOS files, violating the project's ASCII-only rule.
evidence:
`LC_ALL=C grep -n '[^ -~\t]' src/KOKKOS/*` (progress_rules_D/rule7_nonascii.out) reports, besides the citation string in kokkos.cpp:74:
  src/KOKKOS/fix_rigid_small_kokkos.cpp:237  // Host exchange path: flush device->host so the base-class      (U+2192 at column 38)
  src/KOKKOS/fix_rigid_small_kokkos.cpp:688    copy_body_device();  // push host body[] -> d_body            (U+2192 at column 46)
  src/KOKKOS/fix_rigid_small_kokkos.cpp:692  // data to the device - just mark the device side as authoritative and (U+2014 at column 27)
  src/KOKKOS/fix_gjf_kokkos.cpp:132  // vhalf mode: copy lv -> v at start of step (all but the first step)   (U+2192 at column 26)
  src/KOKKOS/atom_vec_ellipsoid_kokkos.cpp:726  // if atom J has bonus data, reset J's bonus.ilocal to loc I      (U+2019 at column 41)
The rule is stated in .github/copilot-instructions.md ('7-bit US-ASCII everywhere ... Unicode is forbidden (security policy)').  `cd src && make check-whitespace check-permissions` passes cleanly, so nothing in the build or CI flags these.
failure_scenario: Compilers and editors on non-UTF-8 locales mangle the comments; the files violate the stated ASCII-only security policy, and a future ASCII CI gate over src/ would fail on the KOKKOS package.
suggested_fix: Replace U+2192 with '->', U+2014 with ' -- ', and U+2019 with a plain apostrophe.

summary: post_force unconditionally calls k_xoriginal.modify_host() before syncing to the device, which makes the (never-updated) host copy of xoriginal win over the device copy and silently overwrites the reference coordinates that the device-side exchange kernels just rewrote.
evidence: fix_spring_self_kokkos.cpp:105-106 'k_xoriginal.modify_host(); k_xoriginal.sync<DeviceType>();' - post_force never writes the host side of k_xoriginal (the kernel at :127-145 only reads d_xoriginal).  Meanwhile pack_exchange_kokkos compacts xoriginal on the device ('d_xoriginal(i,0) = d_xoriginal(j,0); ...' at :197-199) and ends with 'k_xoriginal.template modify<DeviceType>();' (:240), and unpack_exchange_kokkos writes the received values on the device (:261-263) and ends with the same modify (:294); neither touches the host mirror.  For the default double-precision build ttransform_kkfloat_1d_3_lr has NEED_TRANSFORM==0 (kokkos_type.h:700), so modify_host() forwards to Kokkos DualView::modify_host(), which sets modified_flags(0) = max(flags)+1, and sync<DeviceType>() -> sync_device_impl() 'if (modified_flags(0) > modified_flags(1)) { deep_copy(d_view, h_view); ... }' (lib/kokkos/containers/src/Kokkos_DualView.hpp:656-668) - a silent host->device copy of the stale array.  The base class writes xoriginal on the host only in copy_arrays/unpack_exchange/unpack_restart, and each of those KOKKOS overrides already calls modify_host() itself (:175, :322, :352), so the extra unconditional modify_host() serves no purpose.
failure_scenario: GPU build, any run with 'fix spring/self/kk' in which atoms migrate between MPI ranks: comm->exchange() runs before post_force in the same step, so on the first reneighboring step post_force copies the pre-exchange host xoriginal (old local ordering, missing the received atoms) onto the device.  Every atom is then tethered to another atom's reference position, giving wrong forces and a wrong spring energy for the rest of the run.  Even in a single-rank run it forces a full nmax*3 host->device copy every timestep.
suggested_fix: Delete the 'k_xoriginal.modify_host();' at line 105 and keep only 'k_xoriginal.sync<DeviceType>();'.

summary: post_force unconditionally calls k_xoriginal.modify_host() followed by sync<DeviceType>(), so the never-updated host mirror is declared newer and overwrites the device copy that the exchange kernels just wrote - the reference coordinates of migrated atoms are silently reverted.
verified_by: orchestrator (src/KOKKOS/fix_spring_self_kokkos.cpp:105-106; the exchange kernels write d_xoriginal at :189-199 and :261-263 and correctly claim k_xoriginal.modify<DeviceType>() at :240 and :294).

summary: The per-type mass array is read on the device without ever syncing atomKK->k_mass, which is only ever marked modify_host(); on a GPU the kernel therefore reads a zero-initialized device view, massinv becomes infinite and the computed timestep collapses to 0.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/fix_dt_reset_kokkos.cpp:62 syncs only `V_MASK | F_MASK | MASK_MASK | TYPE_MASK | RMASS_MASK` -- there is no mask bit for the per-type mass -- and line 71 then does `mass = atomKK->k_mass.view<DeviceType>();`, used at line 123 `massinv = static_cast<KK_FLOAT>(1.0) / mass[type[i]];` inside the device kernel. `grep -n 'k_mass' src/KOKKOS/fix_dt_reset_kokkos.cpp` yields only that one line: no `k_mass.sync<DeviceType>()` anywhere in the file or its header. k_mass is only ever marked host-modified: src/KOKKOS/atom_kokkos.cpp:313-316 (`create_kokkos(k_mass,mass,ntypes+1,...)` followed by `k_mass.modify_host()`) and the four AtomKokkos::set_mass overloads at atom_kokkos.cpp:287,293,299,305. The required idiom is src/KOKKOS/fix_nve_kokkos.cpp:45-46 `atomKK->k_mass.modify_host(); atomKK->k_mass.sync<DeviceType>();`, also used by compute_temp_kokkos.cpp:46, compute_ke_atom_kokkos.cpp:68, fix_flow_gauss_kokkos.cpp, group_kokkos.h:64 and a dozen others.
failure_scenario: GPU run with a per-type-mass atom style and `fix dt/reset/kk` but no other /kk style that happens to sync k_mass first (e.g. plain `fix nve` without the kk suffix, or `fix nve/limit/kk`, which also never syncs it): the device k_mass view is the zero-filled allocation, so massinv = 1/0 = inf, dtf = sqrt(2*xmax/(ftm2v*sqrt(fsq)*inf)) = 0, dt reduces to 0 and update->dt is set to 0 (or to tmin), stalling the run. With rmass styles the code is unaffected because RMASS_MASK is in the sync list.
suggested_fix: Add `atomKK->k_mass.modify_host(); atomKK->k_mass.template sync<DeviceType>();` to FixDtResetKokkos::init() (or immediately before line 71), exactly as fix_nve_kokkos.cpp:45-46 does.

summary: fix dt/reset/kk divides by a per-type mass read from an unsynced atomKK->k_mass device view.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/fix_dt_reset_kokkos.cpp:62 syncs only `V_MASK | F_MASK | MASK_MASK | TYPE_MASK | RMASS_MASK`, then line 68-71 `if (atomKK->rmass) rmass = ...; else mass = atomKK->k_mass.view<DeviceType>();`, and the kernel does `massinv = 1.0 / mass[type[i]];` (operator()(TagFixDtResetMass), fix_dt_reset_kokkos.cpp:123).  init() (line 49-55) only calls FixDtReset::init() and the respa check; there is no `k_mass.sync<DeviceType>()` in the file.  No MASS_MASK exists in src/atom_masks.h.
failure_scenario: GPU run with per-type masses where k_mass was never synced by another style: massinv = 1/0 = inf, so the computed stable timestep is 0/NaN and `fix dt/reset` resets update->dt to garbage, corrupting the whole trajectory.
suggested_fix: Add `atomKK->k_mass.modify_host(); atomKK->k_mass.sync<DeviceType>();` (the idiom used by FixNVEKokkos::init(), src/KOKKOS/fix_nve_kokkos.cpp:45-46) before the device view is used.

summary: atoms_per_team can become 0 (integer division by zero on the next line) when 'package kokkos threads/per/atom' or 'pair/team/size' is given an unfortunate value; neither is range-checked.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/pair_kokkos.h:926-953: 'if (fpair->lmp->kokkos->threads_per_atom_set) vectorsize = fpair->lmp->kokkos->threads_per_atom; ... vectorsize = MIN(vectorsize,max_vectorsize); ... if (fpair->lmp->kokkos->pair_team_size_set) teamsize_max = fpair->lmp->kokkos->pair_team_size; atoms_per_team = teamsize_max/vectorsize;' followed by line 953 'const int num_teams = inum / atoms_per_team + (inum % atoms_per_team ? 1 : 0);'. The 'if (vectorsize == 0) vectorsize = 1;' guard at line 917 only protects the GetMaxNeighs result, not the later user override. src/KOKKOS/kokkos.cpp:696-706 parses 'threads/per/atom' and 'pair/team/size' with utils::inumeric and no bounds check; KokkosLMP::newton_check (kokkos.cpp:857-870) only checks that neigh/thread is on.
failure_scenario: 'package kokkos neigh/thread on threads/per/atom 0' -> vectorsize 0 -> teamsize_max/0; or 'package kokkos neigh/thread on pair/team/size 8 threads/per/atom 32' -> atoms_per_team = 0 -> inum/0. Either way an integer divide-by-zero (SIGFPE) instead of a clear error message.
suggested_fix: Validate threads_per_atom (>=1) and pair_team_size (>=1) when parsing the package kokkos options, and clamp atoms_per_team to at least 1 in pair_compute_neighlist.

summary: The invalid-neighbor-list fallback uses printf() and then returns silently instead of raising a LAMMPS error.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/pair_kokkos.h:858-865 'EV_FLOAT pair_compute_neighlist (PairStyle* fpair, std::enable_if_t<!((NEIGHFLAG&PairStyle::EnabledNeighFlags) != 0), ...> list) { EV_FLOAT ev; (void) fpair; (void) list; printf("ERROR: calling pair_compute with invalid neighbor list style: requested %i  available %i \n",NEIGHFLAG,PairStyle::EnabledNeighFlags); return ev; }'. .github/copilot-instructions.md forbids printf()/fprintf(screen,...) in favour of utils::logmesg()/error->all().
failure_scenario: A pair style requested with a neighbor list variant it does not support prints an unformatted message on every MPI rank and then computes zero forces silently instead of aborting.
suggested_fix: Replace the printf with fpair->error->all(FLERR, ...) (or utils::logmesg) so the run stops with a proper LAMMPS error message.

summary: pair_kokkos.h dereferences Atom and Force members but includes neither atom.h nor force.h (nor pulls them in transitively), so it compiles only because every including .cpp happens to include them first.
failure_scenario: Any new translation unit that includes pair_kokkos.h (or includes it before atom.h/force.h) and instantiates one of these templates fails to compile with 'invalid use of incomplete type class LAMMPS_NS::Atom'; a header reordering by clang-format/IWYU in an existing pair style .cpp can trigger the same break.
suggested_fix: Add #include "atom.h" and #include "force.h" to the include block at the top of src/KOKKOS/pair_kokkos.h.

summary: Device kernel calls the host math function pow() unqualified instead of Kokkos::pow(), violating KOKKOS rule 4 (all other math in the same block uses Kokkos::).
evidence: src/KOKKOS/pair_tersoff_zbl_kokkos.cpp:406-407 `const KK_FLOAT a_ij = (static_cast<KK_FLOAT>(0.8854)*global_a_0) /\n        static_cast<KK_FLOAT>(pow(d_params(iparam_ij).Z_i,0.23) + pow(d_params(iparam_ij).Z_j,0.23));` inside KOKKOS_INLINE_FUNCTION tersoff_zbl_compute; contrast line 405 `Kokkos::pow(global_e,...)` and lines 411-416 which all use Kokkos::exp. .github/instructions/kokkos.instructions.md rule 4 requires Kokkos:: math in device kernels.
failure_scenario: Compiling tersoff/zbl/kk for a backend whose device math library does not provide an unqualified ::pow overload (SYCL/HIP variants) fails to compile or silently falls back to the host implementation.
suggested_fix: Replace both calls with Kokkos::pow(...); better still, precompute a_ij and premult once per param in setup_params instead of per pair.

summary: Error message in PairTersoffZBLKokkos::init_style names the wrong pair style ("pair tersoff/kk" instead of tersoff/zbl/kk).
evidence: src/KOKKOS/pair_tersoff_zbl_kokkos.cpp:133-134 `if (neighflag == FULL)\n    error->all(FLERR,"Must use half neighbor list style with pair tersoff/kk");` -- copy-paste from src/KOKKOS/pair_tersoff_kokkos.cpp:134-135.
failure_scenario: User runs pair_style tersoff/zbl/kk with `-pk kokkos neigh full` and gets an error naming a style not in the input.
suggested_fix: Name the actual style in the message.

summary: Local `eng` is left uninitialized when eflag==0 but is still passed to ev_tally() when only vflag_either is set.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/pair_tersoff_zbl_kokkos.cpp:422-440: `KK_FLOAT frep, eng;` ... `if (eflag)\n      eng = (1.0 - fermi_k(...)) * eng_z + fermi_k(...) * eng_t;` ... `if (vflag_either || eflag_atom) this->template ev_tally<NEIGHFLAG>(ev,i,j,eng,frep,delx,dely,delz);`. The equivalent code in pair_tersoff_mod_kokkos.cpp:386 computes `eng` unconditionally.
failure_scenario: `compute pressure` without any energy output: EVFLAG=1, eflag=0, vflag_global=1 -> ev_tally is called with an indeterminate `eng`. ev_tally only reads epair under `if (eflag_atom)` (which implies eflag), so no wrong numbers today, but the read of an indeterminate value is fragile and warns under -Wmaybe-uninitialized.
suggested_fix: Initialize `KK_FLOAT eng = 0.0;` (or compute it unconditionally as tersoff/mod does).

summary: The device find_M kernel drops the CPU check that the two atoms found at tag+1 and tag+2 actually have the TIP4P hydrogen type, so a mis-ordered molecule silently produces a wrong M site instead of an error.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/pppm_tip4p_kokkos.cpp:113-122 'int iH1 = AtomKokkos::map_kokkos<DeviceType>(d_tag(i)+1,map_style,k_map_array,k_map_hash); int iH2 = ...(d_tag(i)+2,...); if (iH1 < 0 || iH2 < 0) { k_tip4p_flag...() = 1; ... return; } iH1 = closest_image(i,iH1); iH2 = closest_image(i,iH2);' - only the -1 case is caught.  The CPU base checks both conditions: src/KSPACE/pppm_tip4p.cpp, PPPMTIP4P::find_M(): 'if (iH1 == -1 || iH2 == -1) error->one(FLERR,"TIP4P hydrogen is missing"); if (atom->type[iH1] != typeH || atom->type[iH2] != typeH) error->one(FLERR,"TIP4P hydrogen has incorrect atom type");'.  The same check is present in every other TIP4P implementation (pair_lj_cut_tip4p_long.cpp, pppm_tip4p.cpp).
failure_scenario: A data file whose water molecules are not stored as consecutive O,H,H IDs (e.g. O,H,O,H,... or an ID gap after the O) makes tag+1/tag+2 resolve to non-hydrogen atoms: 'kspace_style pppm/tip4p' aborts with 'TIP4P hydrogen has incorrect atom type', while 'pppm/tip4p/kk' places the M site relative to those unrelated atoms and returns silently wrong long-range energies and forces.
suggested_fix: Add 'if (d_type(iH1) != typeH_kk || d_type(iH2) != typeH_kk) { k_tip4p_flag...() = 2; ... return; }' after the map lookups and report the corresponding error on the host, mirroring the base class.

summary: angle mm3/kk destroys and re-creates the k_eatom/k_vatom dual views on every energy/virial-tally step instead of only when maxeatom/maxvatom grows.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/angle_mm3_kokkos.cpp:72-81: 'if (eflag_atom) { memoryKK->destroy_kokkos(k_eatom,eatom); memoryKK->create_kokkos(k_eatom,eatom,maxeatom,"angle:eatom"); d_eatom = k_eatom.template view<DeviceType>(); } if (vflag_atom) { memoryKK->destroy_kokkos(k_vatom,vatom); ... }'. The sibling styles use the guarded form, e.g. src/KOKKOS/angle_harmonic_kokkos.cpp:74-87 and angle_quartic_kokkos.cpp:68-81: 'if ((int)k_eatom.extent(0) < maxeatom) { destroy; create; d_eatom = ...; } else Kokkos::deep_copy(d_eatom,0.0);'. maxeatom only grows when atom->nmax grows (src/angle.cpp:133-139).
failure_scenario: A run with 'compute pe/atom' or 'compute stress/atom' and thermo output every step frees and re-allocates two device arrays of atom->nmax (and 6*nmax) elements on every tally step; on a GPU this serialises the step behind an allocation and can dominate the angle time.
suggested_fix: Use the same 'if ((int)k_eatom.extent(0) < maxeatom) { ... } else Kokkos::deep_copy(d_eatom,0.0);' pattern as angle_harmonic_kokkos.cpp:74-87.

summary: DomainKokkos::pbc() drops the base class check that owned-atom coordinates are finite, so a blown-up KOKKOS run silently continues with NaN/Inf positions instead of aborting with the documented error.
failure_scenario: A KOKKOS GPU run whose pair style produces an infinite force (two atoms at the same position, bad initial configuration).  On the CPU (or with 'package kokkos comm no') LAMMPS stops with 'Non-numeric atom coords - simulation unstable'; on the device path the NaNs propagate silently and the run ends with garbage output or a much later, unrelated failure.
suggested_fix: Add a Kokkos::parallel_reduce over nlocal that ORs !isfinite(x(i,d)) into a flag (it can be folded into the existing PBC functor as a reduction) and call error->one() with the same message when the flag is set.

summary: fix colvars/kk is a pure delegating wrapper (sync to host, call the CPU hook, mark modified) with no device kernel, which the package's FULL PORTS ONLY rule forbids and which names colvars as the example to leave unported.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/fix_colvars_kokkos.cpp:79-93 is the whole implementation: `post_force` does `atomKK->sync(Host,X_MASK|F_MASK|TAG_MASK|IMAGE_MASK); FixColvars::post_force(vflag); atomKK->modified(Host,F_MASK);` and `end_of_step` likewise; there is no Kokkos kernel anywhere in the file, and the constructor does not even set `execution_space`. .github/instructions/kokkos.instructions.md, section 'FULL PORTS ONLY (project policy)': 'A /kk variant that just syncs to host, calls the CPU base-class hook, and marks modified is a fake port and is forbidden. ... If a fix's per-atom work genuinely cannot run on-device (host-only variable eval, plain double ** arrays like fix move's xoriginal, external library coupling like colvars), leave it unported rather than shipping a delegating wrapper.'
failure_scenario: No numerical error; the styles colvars/kk, colvars/kk/device and colvars/kk/host advertise GPU residency they do not provide, and each post_force forces a full x/f/tag/image device-to-host transfer. Functionally the syncs cover exactly what FixColvars::post_force (src/COLVARS/fix_colvars.cpp:560-563) and ::end_of_step (708-710) read, and setup() is covered because VerletKokkos::setup only clears auto_sync around modify->setup (verlet_kokkos.cpp:196-198) after everything was kept host-current, so this is a policy issue rather than a correctness one.
suggested_fix: Either delete the style per the stated policy, or add an explicit exemption note in the KOKKOS instructions if the maintainers intend to keep it.

summary: pair gauss/kk silently drops the documented 'occupancy' pvector output (nextra set to 0), so a compute pair gauss on the /kk style yields no vector instead of the occupancy count.
failure_scenario: Input using 'pair_style gauss/kk', 'compute gauss all pair gauss', 'variable occ equal c_gauss[1]' -> compute has no vector, so the variable errors out (or silently no data), while the identical non-kk input reports the occupancy.
suggested_fix: Either compute the occupancy count on device (an extra reduction member in EV_FLOAT or a separate parallel_reduce) or, at minimum, print a one-time warning in init_style and document the limitation in doc/src/pair_gauss.rst.
